scenes.narration: We trained a small language model from scratch for Track 01 of the Global Innovation Build Challenge. The rules cap it at fifty million trainable parameters, and ours has 49,822,228. It learned from random weights on 20 billion tokens of openly licensed English text, with our own tokenizer, on one H100 in about eight hours.

slide.title: A 49.8M-parameter language model, trained from scratch

bullets: 49,822,228 trainable parameters, under the 50M cap
20B tokens of openly licensed English text
Our own 32,768-entry byte-level BPE tokenizer
One H100, about 8 hours per main run
No pretrained weights, no synthetic data

scenes.narration: The model is a 14-layer transformer, 512 wide, with grouped-query attention, rotary position embeddings and QK-norm, and a squared ReLU in the MLP. U-net style skips connect early layers to late ones, and a value residual lets every layer reuse the first layer's values. The 32k embedding is tied to the output head and takes a third of the budget. Counted once, as the one tensor the optimizer updates, the total is 49,822,228. Counted twice, it is 66.6 million. We report both.

bullets: Pre-norm decoder, RMSNorm, no biases
GQA: 8 query heads, 4 KV heads, dim 64
RoPE + QK-norm
MLP 512 to 1536 to 512, ReLU²
U-net skips: layer i feeds layer 13 − i
Value residual (ResFormer), 13 learned λ
Logit softcap 15, context 1,024

columns.note: 177,772 under the cap on the counted-once convention. Both conventions are reported in the README.

scenes.narration: Training follows the modded-nanogpt speedrun recipe. Muon updates the matrices inside the blocks, and AdamW updates the embedding and the scalars. The learning rate warms up, holds, then decays to zero over the last 35 percent of training, and at that point the data switches to higher quality sources. We also tried averaging the last few snapshots. It made no difference, so we report the final weights.

bullets: Muon (lr 0.02, Nesterov 0.95) on the 84 block matrices; AdamW (lr 3e-3) on embedding and scalars
Warmup 1%, constant, then linear decay to 0 over the last 35%
524,288 tokens per step: 38,146 steps for 20B tokens
Quality anneal: at decay start, switch to FineWeb-Edu int_score ≥ 4, FineMath, Wikipedia
Checkpoint averaging (last 4 snapshots) tried: no gain, final weights reported
bf16 autocast, torch.compile, single GPU, exact resume

scenes.narration: The data is FineWeb-Edu, DCLM, FineMath, FinePDFs and Wikipedia, all public and openly licensed. WikiText-103 is built from Wikipedia, which is copied all over the web. Before filtering, about five percent of its test 13-grams appeared in a sample of our training data. So we drop every document sharing any 13-gram with WikiText validation or test, 4,969 documents in all, plus 16 Wikipedia articles by title. The multiple-choice benchmarks are not filtered, but their measured overlap is a handful of items.

columns.note: 4,969 documents dropped for sharing a 13-gram with WikiText-103 validation or test, plus 16 Wikipedia articles by title.
Benchmark 13-gram overlap, measured against a 300M-token sample of the filtered training shards. Benchmarks are measured, not filtered.

scenes.narration: Before spending eight GPU-hours on a main run, we ran twelve one-billion-token experiments, each changing one thing. Muon beat AdamW by a wide margin. The value residual gave the biggest perplexity gain, 57.2 down to 54.0, for 13 extra parameters, so we kept it. The quality anneal raised ARC-Easy but lowered PIQA, so our two main runs try two strengths. Each arm is one seed, so benchmark gaps under about two points are noise, and we leaned on perplexity to decide.

slide.title: 12 arms, one change each, one seed

columns.note: WikiText-103 test word perplexity, stride 512. One seed per arm: benchmark gaps under ~2 points are noise.

WinoGrande, {{WINO}} percent. WikiText-103 perplexity, {{WT_LMEVAL}}. {{FINAL_REMARK}} All benchmarks are zero-shot, on the full evaluation sets, with lm-evaluation-harness.

blocks.note: Zero-shot, full evaluation sets, lm-evaluation-harness 0.4.13. Weights: {{WEIGHTS}}. Chance is 25% on HellaSwag and 50% on WinoGrande.

scenes.narration: Now the model itself, running locally on a laptop. We give it three prompts and let it continue. The text is grammatical and keeps the register of the prompt. It also gets facts wrong and repeats itself, which is what we expect at fifty million parameters.

Everything needed to reproduce this is in the repository. uv installs the pinned environment, and the Modal scripts build the data, train and evaluate. On AI use: this project was built with Claude Code agents under human direction. The agents wrote the code, ran the experiments and drafted the docs. Mohammed Alibhai set the goals, made the decisions, reviewed the work and paid for the compute. Thanks for watching.
